lines.trans: Claire! Antoine! Come look at the sidewalk outside our gate!
It is only a quarter to six: are people arriving already?!
The bookshop owner, the pharmacist, the baker's cousin, and twelve neighbors!
All twelve chairs inside Room 9 filled up in three minutes!

words.gram: part of se passer: to happen

lines.trans: Wait: what about those twelve extra folding chairs under the courtyard arch?!
The ones I ordered by mistake last Saturday?!

words.gram: je (I) + ai: 1st person singular present of avoir

lines.trans: Let's unfold all twelve around the four outdoor tables right now!

words.gram: part of tout le monde: everyone

lines.trans: Every single one of your twenty-four half-price chairs has found a guest, Etienne!
Do you hear that, Claire?! My mistake was actually a stroke of genius!

words.gram: subject pronoun, 2nd person, formal (agent to his star)

words.gloss: stroke ('coup de génie' = stroke of genius)
genius ('coup de génie' = stroke of genius)

lines.trans: Take a bow, Etienne, and hand out the menu cards with a smile!
Open the arched windows wide so everyone hears the piano under the linden tree!
Welcome, friends, welcome! Hot mint tea is coming right out!

words.gram: part of tout le monde: everyone

Open the arched windows wide so everyone hears the piano under the linden tree!
Welcome, friends, welcome! Hot mint tea is coming right out!

words.gram: part of tout le monde: everyone

lines.trans: Have a good evening!

meanings.note: A female friend is une amie.

examples.text: C'est un ami très cher.
examples.trans: He is a very dear friend.

examples.text: Mon ami est là.
examples.trans: My friend is here.

meanings.note: Une fenêtre en arc is an arched window. Notice the final -c is pronounced /k/.

examples.text: Les fenêtres en arc donnent sur le jardin intérieur.
examples.trans: The arched windows overlook the inner garden.

examples.text: La pierre forme un bel arc au-dessus de la porte.
examples.trans: The stone forms a lovely arch above the door.

meanings.note: Architectural arch over a passage.

examples.text: Juste sous cette arche. Je vais monter la valise bleue pour vous.
examples.trans: Right under this archway. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

examples.text: Voici l'arche sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the arch, archway on the table.

meanings.note: je viens d'arriver = I've just arrived
Qu'est-ce qui arrive?.

examples.text: Je viens d'arriver à Paris.
examples.trans: I've just arrived in Paris.

examples.text: Le train arrive.
examples.trans: The train is arriving.

meanings.note: No preposition: attendre quelqu'un.
Il vous attend?.

examples.text: Attendez, elle est bleu foncé, exactement comme la vôtre!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

examples.text: Attendez, cette rue est juste ici dans notre quartier, à cinq minutes!
examples.trans: Wait, that street is right here in our neighbourhood, five minutes away!

examples.text: Attendez. Regardez en bas sur la marche en pierre.
examples.trans: Wait. Look down on the stone step.

meanings.note: Used alone (*regarde autour*) or followed by *de* (*autour de la table*, *autour de toi*).

examples.text: Les voisins discutent autour d'une grande théière chaude.
examples.trans: The neighbors chat around a big hot teapot.

examples.text: Regardez autour de vous: tout est propre et rangé.
examples.trans: Look around you: everything is clean and tidy.

examples.text: Tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: You're having lunch with Audiard.

examples.text: Avec plaisir!
examples.trans: With pleasure!

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression.

examples.text: J'ai un petit loft.
examples.trans: I've got a little loft.

examples.text: Tu as une réunion.
examples.trans: You have a meeting.

meanings.note: la bienvenue = the welcome; also used as greeting

examples.text: Bonjour à tous! Bienvenue, Claire. Tout est prêt?
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, Claire. Is everything ready?

examples.text: Bienvenue! Bonjour, madame.
examples.trans: Welcome! Good morning, madam.

examples.text: Bienvenue à l'Hôtel du Tilleul, Claire. Votre deuxième jour ne sera pas ennuyeux.
examples.trans: Welcome to the Hotel du Tilleul, Claire. Your second day will not be boring.

meanings.note: as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day

examples.text: Bon. Alors, je vais attendre.
examples.trans: Fine. Then I'll wait.

examples.text: Ah bon? Il y a un problème avec ma réservation?
examples.trans: Oh really? Is there a problem with my booking?

meanings.note: Masculine boulanger /bulɑ̃ʒe/ drops the final -r sound; feminine boulangère /bulɑ̃ʒɛʁ/ pronounces the -r and opens the vowel.

examples.text: La boulangère ouvre sa boutique à six heures du matin.
examples.trans: The baker opens her shop at six in the morning.

examples.text: Notre boulanger prépare d'excellentes tartes aux pommes.
examples.trans: Our baker makes excellent apple tarts.

meanings.note: Carte de visite.
Carte bancaire.

examples.text: Vous avez la carte, s'il vous plaît?
examples.trans: Do you have the menu, please?

examples.text: Il y a une petite carte en papier attachée à la poignée.
examples.trans: There is a small paper card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: celle = feminine: celle de la semaine dernière

examples.text: Celle de la semaine dernière?
examples.trans: The one from last week?

examples.text: Je prends celui-là.
examples.trans: I'll take that one.

meanings.note: Chacune de ces chaises = each one of these chairs (agrees in gender with the noun it represents, always singular).

examples.text: Chacun des invités reçoit une tasse de thé chaud.
examples.trans: Each of the guests receives a cup of hot tea.

examples.text: Chacune de ces fenêtres donne sur le vieux tilleul.
examples.trans: Each one of these windows overlooks the old linden tree.

meanings.note: A chair; an armchair is un fauteuil.

examples.text: Prends une chaise.
examples.trans: Grab a chair.

examples.text: Quatre tables, huit chaises, tout est en place!
examples.trans: Four tables, eight chairs, everything is in place!

examples.text: Oh... oh non. Où est ma chaise? J'ai les jambes qui tremblent.
examples.trans: Oh... oh no. Where is my chair? My legs are shaking.

meanings.note: Une chambre d'hôtel.
Une chambre d'hôtel.

examples.text: Une chambre au Carlton.
examples.trans: A room at the Carlton.

examples.text: Elle est dans sa chambre.
examples.trans: She's in her room.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'hot'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'hot'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il fait chaud.
examples.trans: It's hot.

examples.text: Un café chaud.
examples.trans: A hot coffee.

examples.text: Il fait chaud. Vous faites quoi?
examples.trans: It's hot. What are you doing?

meanings.en: to order (from a shop, supplier, or café menu)
meanings.note: Everyday verb for placing an order: commander par téléphone ('order by phone'), commander un café.

examples.text: Étienne a commandé des chaises pliantes pour la terrasse.
examples.trans: Étienne ordered folding chairs for the terrace.

examples.text: Nous commandons toujours notre farine au moulin voisin.
examples.trans: We always order our flour from the neighbouring mill.

meanings.en: un coup dur = a hard blow, bad news

examples.text: Un coup de téléphone.
examples.trans: A phone call.

examples.text: Et voilà la cloche du portail. Un coup franc.
examples.trans: There goes the gate bell. One firm ring.

examples.text: Dans la cour.
examples.trans: In the courtyard.

examples.text: Seulement le tilleul de la cour et la pluie.
examples.trans: Only the linden tree in the courtyard and the rain.

meanings.note: Feminine: cousine. Masculine noun ('le cousin', plural 'les cousins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'cousin'.

examples.text: Mon cousin Saïd.
examples.trans: My cousin Saïd.

examples.text: J'ai une idée. Mon cousin Saïd, c'est lui qui conduit dans le film.
examples.trans: I have an idea. My cousin Saïd, he's the one who drives in the film.

examples.text: Chez mon cousin, je l'ai ouverte et j'ai vu des partitions et un ruban rouge.
examples.trans: At my cousin's flat, I opened it and saw sheet music and a red ribbon.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel.
Also 'some': du sucre.

examples.text: Le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: The Kechiche film.

examples.text: C'est du sucre.
examples.trans: It's sugar.

meanings.note: On se retrouve dehors. Invariable French adverb meaning 'outside'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: La boutique a une grande enseigne dehors?
examples.trans: Does the shop have a big sign outside?

examples.text: Gardez la maison, je suis déjà dehors!
examples.trans: Hold the fort, I am already outside!

examples.text: Pas un mot dehors pour l'instant!
examples.trans: Not a word outside for now!

meanings.note: after the noun: la semaine dernière = last week
Before the noun: le dernier jour.

examples.text: Celle de la semaine dernière?
examples.trans: The one from last week?

examples.text: C'est le dernier café.
examples.trans: It's the last coffee.

meanings.en: in front of, before (a place or person)
meanings.note: devant la porte = in front of the door

examples.text: Je t'attends devant le cinéma.
examples.trans: I'll wait for you in front of the cinema.

examples.text: Voilà un taxi devant le portail à l'instant.
examples.trans: Here comes a taxi in front of the gate right now.

meanings.en: to hand out, pass around, distribute
meanings.note: Distribuer le courrier / les menus = hand out the mail / the menus.

examples.text: Il distribue les menus imprimés à chaque table.
examples.trans: He hands out the printed menus to every table.

examples.text: Le facteur distribue le courrier dans notre rue à midi.
examples.trans: The mail carrier delivers mail on our street at noon.

meanings.note: douze heures = twelve o'clock / twelve hours

examples.text: Juste ici! Tout a coûté trente-huit euros, alors voici douze euros de monnaie.
examples.trans: Right here! Everything cost thirty-eight euros, so here is twelve euros in change.

examples.text: Dix, onze, douze. Le compte est bon au centime près, merci!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last cent, thank you!

examples.text: Attendez un instant... Numéro douze, rue des Tilleuls, et deux initiales d'enfant gravées au coin!
examples.trans: Wait a moment... Number twelve, Rue des Tilleuls, and two childhood initials carved in the corner!

meanings.note: Contraction of de + le. In la cause du décès it connects the cause with the death being discussed.
for things you can't count; de la (feminine)

examples.text: C'est du compost.
examples.trans: It's compost.

examples.text: Je veux du pain.
examples.trans: I want some bread.

meanings.note: For something already done.
In a question, can ask about previous experience: tu es déjà venu?

examples.text: Déjà midi!
examples.trans: Midday already!

examples.text: Touchez le tuyau en cuivre! Il chauffe déjà!
examples.trans: Touch the copper pipe! It is warming up already!

examples.text: Gardez la maison, je suis déjà dehors!
examples.trans: Hold the fort, I am already outside!

meanings.en: to unfold (chairs, a tablecloth, a map)
meanings.note: Opposite of plier ('to fold').

examples.text: Déplions six chaises supplémentaires sous l'arbre.
examples.trans: Let's unfold six extra chairs under the tree.

examples.text: Elle déplie une grande nappe blanche sur la table.
examples.trans: She unfolds a big white tablecloth over the table.

en.gloss: in; on; of it; about it; some

meanings.note: Preposition. En retard means late; en vacances means on holiday.
Object pronoun replacing a phrase introduced by de. The English wording depends on the expression: en parler means to talk about it; j'en ai assez means I have had enough.
Object pronoun referring to an unspecified amount or to a quantity named after the action: j'en ai deux means I have two (of them).

examples.text: Je suis en retard.
examples.trans: I'm late.

examples.text: Tu es en vacances?
examples.trans: Are you on holiday?

examples.text: Nous en parlons.
examples.trans: We're talking about it.

meanings.note: je ne veux pas l'entendre = I don't want to hear it

examples.text: Tu entends la musique?
examples.trans: Can you hear the music?

examples.text: Très généreux! Vous avez entendu la cloche du portail en bas?
examples.trans: Very generous! Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?

meanings.note: Une grave erreur. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'blunder, mistake'.

examples.text: Ce tournage était une erreur.
examples.trans: This shoot was a mistake.

examples.text: Quelqu'un à la gare a pris ma valise bleue par erreur!
examples.trans: Someone at the train station took my blue suitcase by mistake!

examples.text: Nous avons noté deux réservations pour la chambre sept par erreur ce soir.
examples.trans: We wrote two bookings for room seven by mistake tonight.

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced.

examples.text: Et vous?
examples.trans: And you?

examples.text: Et demain?
examples.trans: And tomorrow?

meanings.note: In en fait (actually), the final t is pronounced: fɛt.

examples.text: C'est un fait.
examples.trans: It's a fact.

examples.text: En fait, je travaille ici.
examples.trans: Actually, I work here.

meanings.note: Ouvrir / fermer la fenêtre. Feminine noun ('la fenêtre', plural 'les fenêtres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'window'.

examples.text: Regardez, il y a une fenêtre là-haut!
examples.trans: Look, there's a window up there!

examples.text: Elle regarde par la fenêtre.
examples.trans: She looks out the window.

examples.text: Parfait. La fenêtre donne sur la rue ou sur la cour?
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

meanings.note: A plural-only noun. Most following adjectives are masculine plural; certain preceding adjectives can be feminine.

examples.text: Des gens comptent sur ce film.
examples.trans: People are counting on this film.

examples.text: Les gens sont gentils ici.
examples.trans: People are nice here.

examples.text: Parce que le bon café et le pain chaud rendent les gens sympas!
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people friendly!

meanings.note: before the noun: une grande actrice = a great actress
Une grande star.

examples.text: C'est une grande star.
examples.trans: She's a big star.

examples.text: Paris est une grande ville.
examples.trans: Paris is a big city.

meanings.note: Un coup de génie = a stroke of genius.

examples.text: Garder ces chaises pliantes était un vrai coup de génie!
examples.trans: Keeping those folding chairs was a real stroke of genius!

examples.text: Il ne faut pas être un génie pour aimer cette tarte.
examples.trans: You don't have to be a genius to love this tart.

meanings.note: Dans une heure = in an hour.
À quatorze heures = at two pm.

examples.text: À onze heures.
examples.trans: At eleven o'clock.

examples.text: Quelle heure est-il? Neuf heures trente-cinq!
examples.trans: What time is it? Nine thirty-five!

examples.text: Il est là.
examples.trans: He is here.

examples.text: Il y a une réunion.
examples.trans: There is a meeting.

meanings.en: guest (at an event, dinner, or gathering)
meanings.note: Feminine form: une invitée.

examples.text: Chaque invité trouve une chaise autour des tables.
examples.trans: Every guest finds a chair around the tables.

examples.text: Allons accueillir notre première invitée au portail!
examples.trans: Let's go welcome our first guest at the gate!

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel
As a direct-object pronoun: le is masculine, la feminine; both become l' before a vowel sound.

examples.text: Le film est fantastique.
examples.trans: The film is fantastic.

examples.text: La pièce de Koltès.
examples.trans: The Koltès play.

meanings.note: Same form in masculine and feminine: le libraire / la libraire (false friend: librarian is bibliothécaire).

examples.text: La libraire d'à côté nous apporte souvent le courrier.
examples.trans: The bookshop owner next door often brings us the mail.

examples.text: Demandez conseil à la libraire du quartier.
examples.trans: Ask the neighborhood bookseller for advice.

meanings.note: Thé à la menthe = mint tea.

examples.text: Voilà pour vous, madame: du thé chaud à la menthe et du miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea and honey.

examples.text: Voici la menthe sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the mint on the table.

meanings.note: In a French café or bistro, *le menu* often means a fixed-price combination (e.g. soup + tart + tea), while the full list is *la carte*.

examples.text: Le menu de midi propose une soupe chaude et une part de tarte.
examples.trans: The lunch menu offers a hot soup and a slice of tart.

examples.text: Elle écrit le menu du jour à l'encre noire sur un carton.
examples.trans: She writes today's menu in black ink on a card.

meanings.note: Cinq minutes = five minutes.

examples.text: Attendez cinq minutes.
examples.trans: Wait five minutes.

examples.text: J'arrive dans une minute.
examples.trans: I'll be there in a minute.

meanings.note: Moins de trente ans = under thirty.

examples.text: Il est moins grand que moi.
examples.trans: He's shorter than me.

examples.text: Attends au moins une heure.
examples.trans: Wait at least an hour.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la moitié', plural 'les moitiés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'half'.

examples.text: C'est la moitié du travail.
examples.trans: It is half of the work.

examples.text: Couper en deux moitiés.
examples.trans: To cut into two halves.

examples.text: Moitié prix pour ce soir, et le petit-déjeuner offert toute la semaine!
examples.trans: Half price for tonight, and free breakfast all week!

meanings.note: Ma before a feminine noun; mon before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel sound or mute h.

examples.text: Je suis à mon cours.
examples.trans: I'm at my lesson.

examples.text: C'est ma place.
examples.trans: It's my seat.

meanings.note: Final f sounds like /v/ before ans and heures.
Un gilet neuf, une ampoule neuve.

examples.text: C'est à neuf heures.
examples.trans: It's at nine o'clock.

examples.text: J'ai neuf pages à lire.
examples.trans: I have nine pages to read.

examples.text: Vous pouvez? C'est à neuf heures.
examples.trans: Can you make it? It's at nine o'clock.

meanings.note: Plural nos.

examples.text: Deux de nos acteurs.
examples.trans: Two of our actors.

examples.text: C'est notre agence.
examples.trans: It's our agency.

meanings.en: to open (a door, eyes, a book)
meanings.note: conjugated like an -er verb in the present tense: j'ouvre, tu ouvres...

examples.text: Ouvre la porte, Julie!
examples.trans: Open the door, Julie!

examples.text: Le magasin ouvre à neuf heures.
examples.trans: The shop opens at nine o'clock.

meanings.note: Passer par là: to go by there.

examples.text: Par exemple, le contrat de Canet.
examples.trans: For example, Canet's contract.

examples.text: Passe par ici.
examples.trans: Come this way.

meanings.note: Feminine form: une pharmacienne; shop: la pharmacie.

examples.text: Le pharmacien du coin est venu boire un thé à six heures.
examples.trans: The corner pharmacist came for tea at six o'clock.

examples.text: Demandez une bande souple au pharmacien pour votre cheville.
examples.trans: Ask the pharmacist for an elastic wrap for your ankle.

meanings.note: Jouer du piano = to play the piano.

examples.text: Il y a vingt-cinq ans, je donnais des cours de piano près d'ici.
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago, I taught piano lessons near here.

examples.text: Si je connais?! Chaque vendredi pendant six ans, j'ai monté cet escalier en bois pour donner cours de piano!
examples.trans: Do I know it?! Every Friday for six years, I climbed those wooden stairs to teach piano!

examples.text: Un menuisier vivait là avec ses deux petits-fils: l'aîné jouait du piano, et le petit adorait les trains!
examples.trans: A carpenter lived there with his two grandsons: the older boy played piano, and the little one loved trains!

meanings.note: Chaise pliante = folding chair.

examples.text: Vous avez trouvé les trois chaises pliantes derrière la chaufferie, Henri?
examples.trans: Did you find the three folding chairs behind the boiler room, Henri?

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment pliant.
examples.trans: This place is really folding.

meanings.note: With ne: je n'en peux plus.
pronounced plys at the end of a sentence in this sense

examples.text: Il n'est plus là.
examples.trans: He's not here any more.

examples.text: Henri est deux fois plus curieux que nous!
examples.trans: Henri is twice as curious as we are!

meanings.note: Regular plural: les portails.

examples.text: Voilà un taxi devant le portail à l'instant.
examples.trans: Here comes a taxi in front of the gate right now.

examples.text: Vous avez entendu ça, Henri? Quelqu'un vient de sonner au portail!
examples.trans: Did you hear that, Henri? Someone just rang the gate bell!

examples.text: Bonjour, Madame Odette! Regardez ce qui est arrivé au portail hier soir.
examples.trans: Good morning, Madam Odette! Look what arrived at the gate last night.

meanings.note: before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir
+ infinitive: pour voir.

examples.text: Avec moi, toujours! Garde le vous poli pour les clients.
examples.trans: With me, always! Save the polite 'you' for the guests.

examples.text: Juste sous cette arche. Je vais monter la valise bleue pour vous.
examples.trans: Right under this archway. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

examples.text: Deux paires de grandes chaussures marron pour homme et des pulls gris.
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes and grey sweaters.

meanings.note: The amount charged for something.
A prize or award.

examples.text: On vous fait un bon prix.
examples.trans: We'll give you a good price.

examples.text: Il a gagné un prix.
examples.trans: He won a prize.

examples.text: Moitié prix pour ce soir, et le petit-déjeuner offert toute la semaine!
examples.trans: Half price for tonight, and free breakfast all week!

meanings.note: Ouvert au public means 'open to the public'. (As an adjective, masculine public becomes publique in the feminine.)

examples.text: Le jardin de l'hôtel sera ouvert au public le vendredi.
examples.trans: The hotel garden will be open to the public on Fridays.

examples.text: Un nombreux public est venu écouter le concert du soir.
examples.trans: A large audience came to listen to the evening concert.

meanings.note: Et quart = quarter past the hour.

examples.text: Courez vite, Claire. La chambre quatre se réveille à sept heures et quart!
examples.trans: Run fast, Claire. Room four wakes up at quarter past seven!

examples.text: Voici le quart sur la table.
examples.trans: Here is the quarter on the table.

examples.text: À quatre heures du matin.
examples.trans: At four in the morning.

examples.text: J'ai quatre frères.
examples.trans: I have four brothers.

meanings.note: Joins two parts: dis-lui que.
Relative: tout ce que.
With ne: ne... que.
Ça fait trois semaines que.

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.
examples.trans: Tell her I can't come.

examples.text: Je n'ai que deux places.
examples.trans: I've only got two tickets.

meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire') meaning 'to fill up'; essential in everyday spoken and professional French.

examples.text: La salle est déjà bien remplie.
examples.trans: The hall is already well filled.

examples.text: Il remplit son verre d'eau.
examples.trans: He fills his glass of water.

examples.text: Je tourne doucement... écoutez! L'eau remplit le tuyau!

saluer.gloss: to greet; to take a bow

meanings.en: to greet, say hello to; to bow to an audience
meanings.note: Saluer les voisins = greet the neighbors; saluer le public = take a bow.

examples.text: La pianiste et le violoniste saluent le public ensemble.
examples.trans: The pianist and the violinist take a bow together.

examples.text: Elle sort sur le pas de la porte pour saluer les habitués.
examples.trans: She steps out to the doorway to greet the regulars.

meanings.note: Medial -e- is usually dropped in speech (/samdi/). Samedi = 'on Saturday' (this Saturday); le samedi = 'on Saturdays' (habitually).

examples.text: Le grand marché a lieu sur la place chaque samedi matin.
examples.trans: The big market takes place on the square every Saturday morning.

examples.text: La livraison des chaises arrive samedi à quatorze heures.
examples.trans: The delivery of the chairs arrives on Saturday at two p.m.

meanings.note: Reflexive clitic used with third-person subjects; s' before a suitable vowel sound.

examples.text: Il se réveille.
examples.trans: He wakes up.

examples.text: Elle se prépare.

examples.text: J'ai seulement vingt ans.
examples.trans: I'm only twenty.

examples.text: Seulement un café.

meanings.note: pronounced si before a consonant: six jours = si ʒuʁ

examples.text: Six mois.

examples.text: Non, Étienne, le couple du sud est arrivé dans la chambre six il y a une heure.
examples.trans: No, Etienne, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

related.word: pronounced si before a consonant: six jours

meanings.note: Bonne soirée = have a nice evening.

meanings.note: Sous la pluie = in the rain. Core French preposition meaning 'under', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.trans: My hands were cold from the shock!
